nodes.title: Bounded
nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → Prop
nodes.documentation:
`Bounded poset subset` means that `subset` is bounded both above and below
in `poset`.

Logical form:

```lean
BoundedAbove poset subset ∧ BoundedBelow poset subset
```

nodes.title: BoundedAbove
nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → Prop
nodes.documentation:
`BoundedAbove poset subset` means that some candidate in the carrier of
`poset` is an upper bound of `subset`.

Logical form:

```lean
∃ candidate : poset.Carrier,
  UpperBound poset subset candidate
```

nodes.title: BoundedAboveHasUpperBound
nodes.statement:
∀ (poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) {SetObject : Type v}
  [inst : Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] (subset : SetObject),
  LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.BoundedAbove poset subset →
    ∃ candidate, LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.UpperBound poset subset candidate
nodes.documentation:
A set bounded above has an upper bound.

Logical form:

```lean
BoundedAbove poset subset →
  ∃ candidate : poset.Carrier, UpperBound poset subset candidate
```

nodes.title: BoundedAboveIffHasUpperBound
nodes.statement:
∀ (poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) {SetObject : Type v}
  [inst : Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] (subset : SetObject),
  LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.BoundedAbove poset subset ↔
    ∃ candidate, LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.UpperBound poset subset candidate
nodes.documentation:
Bounded above means exactly that an upper bound exists.

Logical form:

```lean
BoundedAbove poset subset ↔
  ∃ candidate : poset.Carrier, UpperBound poset subset candidate
```

nodes.title: BoundedAboveDoesNotImplyGreatestElement
nodes.statement:
LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.BoundedAbove
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo ∧
  ¬∃ maximum,
      LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.GreatestElement
        LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo maximum
nodes.documentation:
Being bounded above does not imply having a greatest element, witnessed
inside the rational numbers by the cut at `√2`.

Logical form:

```lean
FromPartialOrder.BoundedAbove RationalSquareBelowTwo ∧
  ¬ ∃ maximum : Rat,
    FromPartialOrder.GreatestElement RationalSquareBelowTwo maximum
```

nodes.title: BoundedAboveDoesNotImplyLeastUpperBound
nodes.statement:
LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.BoundedAbove
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo ∧
  ¬∃ supremum,
      LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.LeastUpperBound
        LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo supremum
nodes.documentation:
Being bounded above does not imply possessing a least upper bound inside
an arbitrary poset, witnessed by the rational cut at `√2`.

Logical form:

```lean
FromPartialOrder.BoundedAbove RationalSquareBelowTwo ∧
  ¬ ∃ supremum : Rat,
    FromPartialOrder.LeastUpperBound RationalSquareBelowTwo supremum
```

nodes.title: RationalAboveSqrtTwoIsUpperBound
nodes.statement:
∀ (candidate : ℚ),
  √2 < ↑candidate →
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.UpperBound
      LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo candidate
nodes.documentation:
Every rational strictly above `√2` is an upper bound of the rationals
whose squares are below two.

Logical form:

```lean
Real.sqrt 2 < (candidate : Real) →
  FromPartialOrder.UpperBound RationalSquareBelowTwo candidate
```

nodes.title: RationalSquareBelowTwo
nodes.statement: Set ℚ
nodes.documentation:
The rational numbers whose squares are strictly less than two.

Logical form:

```lean
{rational : Rat | rational ^ 2 < 2}
```

nodes.title: RationalSquareBelowTwoCanAlwaysIncrease
nodes.statement:
∀ rational ∈ LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo,
  ∃ larger ∈ LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo, rational < larger
nodes.documentation:
Every rational whose square is below two has a strictly larger rational
whose square is still below two.

Logical form:

```lean
∀ rational ∈ RationalSquareBelowTwo,
  ∃ larger ∈ RationalSquareBelowTwo, rational < larger
```

nodes.title: RationalSquareBelowTwoHasNoGreatestElement
nodes.statement:
¬∃ maximum,
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.GreatestElement
      LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo maximum
nodes.documentation:
The rationals whose squares are below two have no greatest element.

Logical form:

```lean
¬ ∃ maximum : Rat,
  FromPartialOrder.GreatestElement RationalSquareBelowTwo maximum
```

nodes.title: RationalSquareBelowTwoHasNoLeastUpperBound
nodes.statement:
¬∃ supremum,
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.LeastUpperBound
      LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo supremum
nodes.documentation:
The rationals whose squares are below two have no rational least upper
bound: any proposed rational supremum would have to equal the irrational
number `√2`.

Logical form:

```lean
¬ ∃ supremum : Rat,
  FromPartialOrder.LeastUpperBound RationalSquareBelowTwo supremum
```

nodes.title: RationalSquareBelowTwoHasUpperBoundTwo
nodes.statement:
LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.FromPartialOrder.UpperBound
  LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Counterexamples.RationalSquareBelowTwo 2
nodes.documentation:
Two is an upper bound of the rationals whose squares are below two.

Logical form:

```lean
FromPartialOrder.UpperBound RationalSquareBelowTwo (2 : Rat)
```

nodes.title: LraRealOfReal
nodes.statement: ℝ → LRA.VolumeIII.RealNumbers.LraReal
nodes.documentation:
Wrap a Mathlib real as the LRA lower Dedekind cut of rationals below it.

Logical form:

```lean
{q : Rat | (q : Real) < value}
```

nodes.title: LraRealOfRealMonotone
nodes.statement:
∀ {left right : ℝ},
  left ≤ right →
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Examples.LraRealOfReal left ≤
      LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.Examples.LraRealOfReal right
nodes.documentation:
Wrapping Mathlib reals as LRA lower cuts preserves their order.

Logical form:

```lean
left ≤ right → LraRealOfReal left ≤ LraRealOfReal right
```

nodes.title: SquareBelowTwo
nodes.statement: Set ℝ
nodes.documentation:
The real numbers whose squares are strictly less than two.

Logical form:

```lean
{x : Real | x ^ 2 - 2 < 0}
```

nodes.title: WrappedSquareBelowTwo
nodes.statement: Set LRA.VolumeIII.RealNumbers.LraReal
nodes.documentation:
The image in `LraReal` of the real numbers whose squares are strictly less
than two.

Logical form:

```lean
LraRealOfReal '' {x : Real | x ^ 2 - 2 < 0}
```

nodes.title: GreatestElement
nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → poset.Carrier → Prop
nodes.documentation:
`GreatestElement poset subset candidate` means that `candidate` belongs
to `subset` and is an upper bound of `subset`.

Logical form:

```lean
candidate ∈ subset ∧ UpperBound poset subset candidate
```

nodes.title: GreatestElementIsBelowLeastUpperBound
nodes.statement:
∀ (poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) {SetObject : Type v}
  [inst : Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] (subset : SetObject)
  (maximum supremum : poset.Carrier),
  LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.GreatestElement poset subset maximum →
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.LeastUpperBound poset subset supremum →
      poset.NonStrictOrder maximum supremum
nodes.documentation:
Every least upper bound is above every greatest element of the same set.

Logical form:

```lean
GreatestElement poset subset maximum →
  LeastUpperBound poset subset supremum →
  poset.NonStrictOrder maximum supremum
```

nodes.title: GreatestElementIsMember
nodes.documentation:
A greatest element (maximum) belongs to the set.

Logical form:

```lean
GreatestElement poset subset maximum → maximum ∈ subset
```

  LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.GreatestElement poset subset maximum →
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.UpperBound poset subset maximum
nodes.documentation:


nodes.title: GreatestLowerBound
nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → poset.Carrier → Prop
nodes.documentation:
`GreatestLowerBound poset subset candidate` means that `candidate` is a
lower bound of `subset` above every other lower bound.

Logical form:

```lean
LowerBound poset subset candidate ∧
  ∀ otherCandidate : poset.Carrier,
    LowerBound poset subset otherCandidate →
    poset.NonStrictOrder otherCandidate candidate
```

nodes.title: HasUpperBoundImpliesBoundedAbove
nodes.statement:
∀ (poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) {SetObject : Type v}

  (∃ candidate, LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.UpperBound poset subset candidate) →
    LRA.Pilot.OrderBounds.BoundedAbove poset subset
nodes.documentation:
The existence of an upper bound makes a set bounded above.

Logical form:

```lean

  BoundedAbove poset subset
```


nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → poset.Carrier → Prop
nodes.documentation:

Logical form:

```lean
    UpperBound poset subset otherCandidate →
    poset.NonStrictOrder candidate otherCandidate
```

nodes.title: LowerBound
nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → poset.Carrier → Prop
nodes.documentation:
`LowerBound poset subset candidate` means that `candidate` is related to
every member of `subset` by the partial order carried by `poset`.

Logical form:

```lean
∀ element : poset.Carrier,
  element ∈ subset → poset.NonStrictOrder candidate element
```

nodes.title: MaximalElement
nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → poset.Carrier → Prop
nodes.documentation:
`MaximalElement poset subset candidate` means that `candidate` belongs to
`subset` and every member of `subset` above it is equal to it.

Logical form:

```lean
candidate ∈ subset ∧
  ∀ element : poset.Carrier,
    element ∈ subset →
    poset.NonStrictOrder candidate element →
    element = candidate
```

```lean
  ∀ element : poset.Carrier,
```

nodes.title: PartialOrderFromPoset
nodes.statement: (poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) → PartialOrder poset.Carrier
nodes.documentation:
`PartialOrderFromPoset poset` exposes an explicit LRA poset as a Lean partial
order on its carrier. Install it locally with `letI` when typeclass-driven
Mathlib declarations should use `poset.NonStrictOrder` as `≤`.

Logical form:

```lean
_root_.PartialOrder poset.Carrier where
  le := poset.NonStrictOrder
  le_refl := poset.NonStrictOrderIsPartialOrder.1
  le_antisymm := poset.NonStrictOrderIsPartialOrder.2.1
  le_trans := poset.NonStrictOrderIsPartialOrder.2.2
```

nodes.title: PosetFromPartialOrder
nodes.statement: (carrier : Type u) → [partialOrder : PartialOrder carrier] → LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset
nodes.documentation:
`PosetFromPartialOrder carrier` packages Lean's inferred partial order on
`carrier` as an explicit LRA poset.

Logical form:

```lean
Poset where
  Carrier := carrier
  NonStrictOrder := (· ≤ ·)
  NonStrictOrderIsPartialOrder := ⟨le_refl, le_antisymm, le_trans⟩
```

nodes.statement:
(poset : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Order.Poset) →
  {SetObject : Type v} → [Membership poset.Carrier SetObject] → SetObject → poset.Carrier → Prop
nodes.documentation:
`UpperBound poset subset candidate` means that every member of `subset`
is related to `candidate` by the partial order carried by `poset`.

Logical form:

```lean
∀ element : poset.Carrier,
  element ∈ subset → poset.NonStrictOrder element candidate
```

nodes.title: Poset
nodes.statement: Type (u + 1)
nodes.documentation:
A poset is a carrier equipped with a partial order.

Logical form:

```lean
structure Poset where
  Carrier : Type u
  NonStrictOrder : LRA.VolumeI.Relations.Endorelation Carrier
  NonStrictOrderIsPartialOrder : PartialOrder NonStrictOrder
```
